name: TagGroup
purpose: Lays out a wrapping row of Tags with an optional overflow tag that opens a Dropdown Menu holding whichever tags got truncated.
intent: A thin composition of Tag (every visible tag and the overflow tag itself) and Dropdown Menu (the overflow panel), preconfigured for the bounded-tag-list-with-overflow use case, rather than a third independent implementation of wrapping-row layout or floating-panel behavior.
tierNote: Classified as a molecule, but its overflow panel composes Dropdown Menu (an organism, itself built from Menu + Popup) - a deliberate, documented exception to CLAUDE.md's 'molecules compose only from atoms/primitives' rule, not an oversight. Rejected alternatives: re-implementing a lighter Popup-only panel (would duplicate Menu's row/keyboard-navigation behavior), or reclassifying Dropdown Menu/Menu down to molecules (a larger, unrelated change).

sourceFiles.note: tag-group.module.css contains exactly one rule (the wrapping row layout + gap) - every other visible pixel comes from Tag's own tone/size styling and Dropdown Menu/Menu's panel/row styling.

figmaSource.note: The real Figma component set is named tab-group, not tag-group - a naming typo, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. It is filed on the file's own "✅ Tag Group" page, and every variant is unambiguously a wrapping row of `tag` instances plus an eleventh `tag` (reading "+5 more") nested inside a `dropdown-menu` instance's trigger slot - not tabs. Code follows the real, verified structure under the correct name, TagGroup.
figmaSource.structure: Four variants cross two axes: `size` (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) x `alignment`. Each variant is an auto-layout frame (layoutWrap: WRAP, itemSpacing: 8, counterAxisSpacing: 8, counterAxisAlignItems: CENTER) containing ten `tag` instances (tone=standard/default, isRemovable=false, elemBefore=false, text "Tag") plus one `dropdown-menu` instance (trigger=tag, alignment=left, isOpen=false) whose trigger slot holds an eleventh `tag` instance reading "+5 more" (same variant shape as the others: tone=standard, isRemovable=false). Every `tag` instance inside a variant - the ten visible ones and the overflow trigger's - carries that variant's own size, so size is uniform per group with no per-tag mixing. Measured frame heights match the size axis exactly (sm: 24, md: 32). In `alignment=left`, the dropdown-menu instance is the last child (trailing); in `alignment=right`, it is the first child (leading). The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property measures `left` in every case - it does not flip with the outer variant.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's example is a fixed illustrative count (10 visible tags + a "+5 more" overflow tag = 15 total, with no exposed count/list-editing property). Code generalizes this into an open, data-driven `tags: TagGroupItem[]` array plus a `maxVisible` number, the same 'closed demo becomes an open prop' adaptation Menu made for its own `sections` versus Figma's per-variant row instances.

Figma's `alignment` variant (left/right) became TagGroupProps.alignment directly, unchanged in name or values - it controls only where the overflow tag renders (trailing vs. leading), not which tags are visible or truncated, matching the fact that every Figma variant shows the identical placeholder tag set.

Figma's `size` axis (`sm (24)` / `md (32)`) became TagGroupProps.size, carrying Tag's own TagSize values (sm/md) rather than Figma's parenthesised pixel labels. It applies uniformly to every visible tag and to the overflow tag, because that is what Figma does inside each variant - so TagGroupItem omits `size` from Tag's own props entirely. TagGroup defaults to `sm`, a deliberate divergence from Tag's own `md` code default: `size=sm (24)` is the first variant in Figma's grid and the one its illustrative examples use.

The nested dropdown-menu's own `alignment` property was measured as `left` in both outer `alignment` variants (not flipped for `alignment=right`) - code matches this directly: TagGroup always renders the overflow tag's DropdownMenu with Dropdown Menu's own default alignment (left), rather than deriving or flipping it from TagGroup's own `alignment` prop.

The overflow tag's trigger needed a plain, focusable, non-navigational, non-removable interactive form - a gap in Tag's own code API (Tag was previously focusable only via `href` or its remove button). Added `isInteractive` to Tag itself (see tag.contract.json's own apiAdaptationNotes) rather than reimplementing a one-off interactive wrapper inside Tag Group.

Figma's nested `dropdown-menu` instance has an empty `content` slot in the static file (isOpen=false, never toggled open in the source), so the overflow panel's actual content (a Menu row per truncated tag) is a code-level design decision, not something measured from an open Figma variant - informed directly by Dropdown Menu's own established 'always renders a Menu built from sections' rule.

useCases: A bounded list of entity-reference tags on a record detail view, with the rest reachable via "+N more"
An active-filters row that can grow past what comfortably fits on one line
A short, unbounded tag list with no truncation at all (maxVisible omitted)
antiPatterns: A single tag - use Tag directly
A group of Buttons - use Button Group

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: A wrapping flex row (gap: spacing-sm) - the only styling Tag Group owns.

anatomy.name: visible tags
anatomy.description: tags.slice(0, maxVisible) (or every tag, when maxVisible is omitted), each a real Tag with every one of its own props forwarded, size applied uniformly.

anatomy.name: overflow tag
anatomy.description: Present only when tags.length > maxVisible. A Tag with isInteractive (Tag's plain-button form) reading overflowLabel(hiddenTags.length), wrapped in a DropdownMenu.

anatomy.name: overflow panel
anatomy.description: Dropdown Menu's Menu, one section (id: 'overflow') with one MenuItem per truncated tag - label, a decorative leadingElement from that tag's own elemBefore, and disabled mirroring that tag's own isDisabled.

tags.description: Every tag, visible and truncated. Each item is Tag's own props (minus size/children/isInteractive) plus a required id and a label (forwarded to Tag as children).

maxVisible.description: Once tags.length exceeds this, only the first maxVisible tags render - the rest are truncated behind the overflow tag. No truncation, and no overflow tag, when omitted.

size.description: Applied uniformly to every rendered tag, including the overflow tag.

alignment.description: Where the overflow tag renders relative to the visible tags - trailing (left) or leading (right). Does not change which tags are visible or truncated.

overflowLabel.description: The overflow tag's text, given the truncated count.

overflowMenuAriaLabel.description: Accessible name for the overflow panel (forwarded to Dropdown Menu's aria-label, then to Menu's role="menu" container).

onOverflowTagSelect.description: Called when a truncated tag is selected from the overflow panel. Tag Group does not navigate, remove, or close the panel on its own.

id.description: Applied to the root row element.

className.description: Composes with the root row element's class list.

left.purpose: Visible tags first, overflow tag trailing - matches Figma's default.

right.purpose: Overflow tag first (leading), then the visible tags.

accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the overflow tag by Popup (via Dropdown Menu), reflecting the panel's open state
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the overflow tag by Popup, pointing at the panel id while open
accessibility.overflowPanelRole: menu (set by Menu, via Dropdown Menu), named by overflowMenuAriaLabel
accessibility.visibleTagAccessibility: unchanged from Tag's own documented accessibility - Tag Group applies no ARIA of its own to visible tags

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves between visible tags (per their own navigability) and the overflow tag, in DOM order
Enter/Space activates the overflow tag (native button behavior, inherited from Tag's isInteractive form)
Escape closes the open overflow panel (inherited from Popup, via Dropdown Menu)
Arrow keys/Home/End/Enter navigate and activate rows inside the open overflow panel (inherited from Menu)
behaviorRules: hasOverflow = typeof maxVisible === 'number' && tags.length > maxVisible - the overflow tag renders only then.
visibleTags = hasOverflow ? tags.slice(0, maxVisible) : tags; hiddenTags = hasOverflow ? tags.slice(maxVisible) : [].
alignment only reorders the overflow tag relative to the visible tags - it never changes the visibleTags/hiddenTags split.
Holds exactly one piece of state (overflowOpen) to drive the overflow DropdownMenu, which is itself fully controlled.
Never calls onOverflowTagSelect's implied navigation/removal automatically, and never closes the overflow panel on selection - only calls the callback itself, exactly like a Menu item's onSelect.
Does not forward its own alignment prop to the nested DropdownMenu - always uses DropdownMenu's own default (left), matching the measured Figma value in both tab-group variants.
compositionRules: Pass every tag's own props (tone, href, isRemovable, onRemove, elemBefore, ...) directly on each TagGroupItem - they forward straight to the rendered Tag.
Do not set size per item - TagGroupItem omits it from Tag's own props; Tag Group applies one size uniformly.
Wire onOverflowTagSelect when truncated tags need to be reachable (navigate, remove, etc.) - Tag Group does nothing with a selection on its own.
responsiveRules: The root row wraps at any container width, identical to a plain flex-wrap layout.
The overflow panel inherits Popup's resize/scroll-driven repositioning and touch-friendly outside-dismissal identically to Dropdown Menu.
themeRules: Inherits Tag's and Dropdown Menu/Menu's token-driven theming - no component-level light/dark branching of its own.

tokens.note: tag-group.module.css declares exactly one token reference - gap: var(--spacing-sm), matching Figma's measured 8px itemSpacing/counterAxisSpacing on both axes of the wrap layout. Every other value is Tag's own tone/size tokens or Dropdown Menu/Menu's own panel/row tokens - see their respective contract.json files.

do: Pass every tag's own props directly on each TagGroupItem rather than constructing a separate Tag element.
Wire onOverflowTagSelect when a truncated tag needs to do something when selected.
dont: Do not set size on an individual TagGroupItem - it is omitted from the type; set it once on TagGroupProps.
Do not expect selecting a truncated tag to navigate, remove, or close the panel automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders every tag with no overflow tag when maxVisible is omitted or tags.length <= maxVisible.
Renders tags.slice(0, maxVisible) plus an overflow tag reading overflowLabel(hiddenCount) when tags.length > maxVisible.
alignment=left (default) renders the overflow tag after the visible tags; alignment=right renders it before them - in both cases the same tags are visible.
Activating the overflow tag opens a role="menu" panel listing every truncated tag as a menuitem row.
Selecting a truncated tag calls onOverflowTagSelect(tag, event) and does not close the panel or perform navigation/removal on its own.
Applies size uniformly to every visible tag and the overflow tag.
Supports a custom id/className on the root and a custom overflowLabel/overflowMenuAriaLabel.
knownLimitations: No built-in virtualization - a very large tags array renders every visible tag eagerly, same as Menu's own sections.
Inherits every one of Dropdown Menu's and Menu's own knownLimitations for the overflow panel (no typeahead, no built-in focus-first-item-on-open).
futureEnhancements: A count-only overflow mode (numeric badge instead of a full Tag) for very dense layouts.
A renderTag/renderOverflowItem escape hatch for fully custom row content, if a real use case needs it.
